svg.aria-label: Queen and Kafka at 3 million messages a second from 10 to 10 million partitions: end to end latency, broker CPU, memory and disk writes
svg.text: Queen 2.3.0 and Kafka 4.3.1 at 1M msg/s of 1 KB messages, one queue or topic, 10 to 10M partitions
The same six GCP VMs: three c4-standard-24-lssd brokers (24 vCPU, 88 GB, four local NVMe disks in RAID0), three 16-vCPU loaders · 2026-10-14

svg.text: CPU, cores of the three brokers (of 72)
Memory of the busiest broker, GB (of 88)
Fresh cluster a point, 70 s of load, 100 JSON messages of 1 KB a request (1,027 B), nine load processes; otherwise the settings of the 3M matrix.
Kafka: three replicas, acks=all, min.insync 2, idempotent producer, lz4, linger 5 ms, 6 GB heap; writes go to the page cache (no fsync per write);
XFS noatime, 24 request handler, 12 network and 12 replica fetcher threads, writeback from 1 GB of dirty pages (on ext4 its p99 was up to ten times higher).
Kafka between the drawn counts: 25k partitions carried, p50 / p99 15 / 45 ms on 56 cores; 50k not carried (159k msg/s pushed); Queen not run there.
Queen on ext4 noatime, writeback from 5% of RAM (XFS gave it no gain): a write is answered after the leader's fsync and one follower's;
binary push, zstd, counts acks, framed pops, dedup off; 10M partitions with QUEEN_CONSUME_IDLE_UNLOAD_S=30.
Kafka's memory leaves out the page cache it reads from.
